cases.resource_analysis: The frozen sources declare distinct logical contracts, but none activates them. QoS would reorder scheduler requests, unified communication would select worker communication behavior, and observability would attach scheduler/worker callbacks plus optional files and a writer thread.
cases.authority_analysis: Host authority is retained for the token budget, GroupCoordinator/process groups, transfer lifecycle, and shared event registry. No source claims a second token budget, process group, or transfer owner.
cases.process_carrier_analysis: All three request vLLM process carriers and overlap at least in the engine/worker topology, but the manifests do not identify concrete process instances or a host provider that wires all three.
cases.ordering_analysis: No pinned source specifies joint policy registration, callback dispatch, shutdown, or failure ordering. QoS explicitly requires fail-closed activation for untested KV-disaggregation combinations, while the observability host seam is unimplemented.
cases.reason: The sources rule out a proven static exclusive-owner collision but do not establish a runnable joint carrier or safe lifecycle order. Admit and reject would both exceed the evidence.

cases.resource_analysis: The packages describe communication selection, split-batch graph planning, and transfer observation. Their logical resources differ, but the future implementations converge on worker execution, streams/collectives, transfer callbacks, graph context, and teardown.
cases.authority_analysis: Core GroupCoordinator retains communicator authority, the Ascend host must own graph pools/execution, and the host owns transfer lifecycle/event dispatch. The plugins remain policy/observer proposals.
cases.process_carrier_analysis: The unified and observability manifests target generic vLLM processes while split-batch targets vllm-ascend worker/device paths. No exact core/Ascend host tuple or carrier map is bound for the composition.
cases.ordering_analysis: No pinned source defines ordering between collective selection, split execution/context restoration, first-compute/transfer callbacks, and shutdown. All three host attachment paths are absent or proposal-only.
cases.reason: Distinct declared contracts are insufficient to prove compatibility across a shared worker/device carrier. There is also no source-proven exclusive collision, so the independent decision is abstain.
